summary_html: Agency chooses **Differential Response (DR)**/**Alternative Response**: engage **services without court petition** when safety permits. FFPSA and IV-B/IV-E prevention funding support voluntary, front-end help to avert removals.
authority_html:
- **Family First Prevention Services Act (FFPSA)** — prevention services framework under IV-E  
- **SSA Title IV-B & IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 620–629m; 670–679c)** — service funding & case-plan requirements  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — assesses safety/permanency outcomes in DR systems

key_cases.case_name: Clark County v. Eighth Judicial District Court (Eggleston)
key_cases.holding: Qualified immunity and Nevada discretionary-act immunity barred suit against a county social worker who allegedly coerced a parent into signing temporary guardianship papers placing his children with relatives instead of filing a petition.
key_cases.relevance: The leading recent Nevada case on the alternative-response path of a 'voluntary' relative placement in lieu of a petition.
key_cases.quote: we consider whether qualified and discretionary-act immunity apply to bar suit against a social worker who allegedly coerced a parent to sign guardianship papers

key_cases.case_name: Capp v. County of San Diego
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
key_cases.holding: A social worker who threatens to terminate a parent's custody in retaliation for the parent's protected criticism of the agency violates the First Amendment, and is not entitled to qualified immunity.
key_cases.relevance: A 'voluntary' alternative-response agreement obtained under threat of removal is constitutionally suspect.
key_cases.quote: A reasonable official would have known that taking the serious step of threatening to terminate a parent's custody of his children

key_cases.case_name: Washoe County Department of Social Services v. Kory L.G.
key_cases.holding: A non-offending parent — one not found to have abused or neglected the child — cannot be compelled to comply with an NRS 432B.560 case plan as a condition of reunification, and the agency's reasonable-efforts duty under NRS 432B.393 runs regardless.
key_cases.relevance: Supports handling a non-offending parent outside the coercive petition track.
key_cases.quote: the agency must make reasonable efforts to reunify and preserve the family of the child, with the child's health and safety being a paramount concern

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: A fit parent's decisions about the care, custody and control of his or her children are presumed to be in the children's best interests, and a court may not override them merely because it would decide differently.
key_cases.relevance: Alternative response must respect parental decision-making absent a finding of unfitness.
key_cases.quote: there is a presumption that fit parents act in the best interests of their children

timeline_requirements.deadline: As part of an investigation initiated pursuant to NRS 432B.260 the agency must determine, first in the order of priority set by the rule, whether the child is safe considering the factors set forth in NAC 432B.160; no separate deadline is set for that determination (NAC 432B.150(2)). The child must be seen immediately if the allegations suggest imminent harm (NAC 432B.150(3)(b)), and where the investigation was initiated by telephone or a review of a case record a face-to-face meeting with the child and his family must be attempted on the next business day and on each successive business day until the supervisor of the case manager of the case determines that a resolution has been achieved (NAC 432B.155(1))
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Investigation initiated by the agency which provides child welfare services pursuant to NRS 432B.260
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in NAC 432B.150 or NAC 432B.155
